summary: Forest Service lookout at 1,180 m in Bulkley-Nechako; a 1991 item has a lookout attendant on it and a 2015 notice describes the drive up.

access.note: A 2015 visitor notice describes a drive up a forest service road and invites visitors. No later source found; confirm before a visit.

visit.trail_note: Ferry across Francois Lake off Highway 35, then 11 km and another 12 km of road, a turn onto the Verdun Lookout Forest Service Road, and about 2 km of sometimes rough access road to the lookout (2015 notice).

events.note: Lake District News item of May 1991, quoted on Canada's Fire Lookouts, says Daphne Ewart was once again on the Verdun Lookout and welcomed company.

evidence.supports: Verdun listing places the site in Bulkley-Nechako
Verdun Forest Service Lookout, about 49 km south of a town the notice does not name
evidence.quote: Located approximately 49 kms south of town, Verdun Forest Service Lookout has amazing views in every direction.

evidence.supports: Daphne Ewart back on the Verdun Lookout
evidence.quote: Daphne Ewart has returned to the Southside and is once again on the Verdun Lookout.
She welcomes company at her lookout

evidence.supports: Route: ferry across Francois Lake off Highway 35
evidence.quote: To get there, follow Hwy 35 and take the ferry across Francois Lake.

evidence.supports: About 2 km of sometimes rough access road
evidence.quote: continue for approximately 2 kms on a sometimes rough access road.

evidence.supports: After the ferry, 11 km on Keefe's Landing Road
Another 12 km, then a turn onto the Verdun Lookout Forest Service Road
evidence.quote: Drive for another 12 kms and turn right onto Verdun Lookout Forest Service Road
Once up at the lookout, you can see from the Uncha/Binta Valley to Francois Lake; all the way to sweeping views of Ootsa Lake and Tweedsmuir Park.

evidence.supports: Notice calls it a destination for all ages
evidence.quote: An enjoyable afternoon adventure, Verdun Forest Service Lookout is the perfect destination for young and old alike.

sources.title: Verdun Lookout – great place to visit

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder or design found in any source reached; the record's built status is unknown. The 2015 notice is the newest source and describes a visit, not the structure's condition: confirm that a lookout still stands and that the road is open before publishing. The 1991 staffing item is read only through the quote on Canada's Fire Lookouts; the newspaper original was not checked. The notice says 'town' without naming it; the story no longer names Burns Lake, because the paper's name does not establish which town is meant. The listing prints 'Elev. 1180' with no unit; metres are assumed, as for Uncha. Not linked to the lookout: an August 2018 Verdun Mountain wildfire (Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako evacuation order, rescinded 12 September 2018). No source ties that fire to the lookout, so it is left out. BC Archives could not be searched from the cached reader (certificate error).
